newsitem.title: TOGO: Ailing Mobutu prolongs Togo stay on health grounds.
newsitem.headline: Ailing Mobutu prolongs Togo stay on health grounds.

text.p: Zaire's ailing and ousted president Mobutu Sese Seko prolonged his stay in the West African state of Togo on health grounds on Tuesday after his flight into exile left him "very, very weak", a source close to the government said.
The veteran strongman, who is fighting cancer, arrived in the Togolese capital on Sunday night on a Russian-made cargo plane from his jungle palace Gbadolite in northern Zaire.
One unconfirmed report on Togo television on Sunday said that Mobutu had to leave Gbadolite in a hurry and that rebels fired on the plane as it took Mobutu on the first leg of his flight into exile.
The source close to the government said that Mobutu had initially landed in Togo for a technical stopover but that the government had agreed to let him stay longer because of his state of health.

Mobutu, who ruled Africa's third largest country for over three decades, left his capital Kinshasa on Friday, one day before Laurent Kabila's rebels marched in triumphantly and virtually unopposed after seven months of civil war.
The tiny West African coastal state of Togo is ruled by Mobutu's friend Gnassingbe Eyadema, another veteran African strongman who took power at around the same time.
